name: Ivan Carter McIndoo House

dates.altered: Moved from 410 North Van Ness Avenue to 310 North Fulton Street; the survey dates the relocation 'ca. 1992' and records a one-storey room addition on the northwest facade 'likely added after' it.
dates.note: The survey: 'Date of erection: ca. 1913', 'Architect: Unknown'.

refs.title: IVAN CARTER MCINDOO HOUSE HABS CA-2885 310 North Fulton Street (Moved from 410 North Van Ness Avenue) Fresno Fresno County California
refs.note: The survey number is read from the data page's own header and running heads ('IVAN CARTER MCINDOO HOUSE HABS No. CA-2885 (Page 13)'). The data page also records that the house 'was determined eligible for inclusion in the National Register of Historic Places through consensus determination' and is on the City of Fresno local register as 'the McIndoo-Phillips Home (H.P. #204)'; no National Register number exists to record.
The item id is the path segment of the data PDF actually fetched; the landing page itself was not opened.

quotes.text: 1. Architectural Character: The Ivan Carter McIndoo house was constructed near the end of North Park‘s residential development, and near the end of the Arts and Crafts movement that had inspired its distinctive creation of place. The house represents the aesthetics of a natural Craftsman bungalow, as applied to larger dwellings ca. 1913 and often called the ―bungaloid‖ form.

1. Overall dimensions: The two-and-a-half story, side-gable house has a simple rectangular ground plan with a less-than-room-sized irregular projection in the southeast corner of the house. The house is two bays wide and three bays deep.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885, Part II.B.1; between the '(Page 10)' and '(Page 12)' markers, no nearer one legible

quotes.text: 2. Foundation: The house has a vented pier and beam foundation. No sill treatment is visible because shingling extends to the ground‘s edge.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885, Part II.B.2; same span

quotes.text: There is a cantilevered screened-in sleeping porch on the north façade‘s second story. The sleeping porch is supported by wood board piers and a wood knee bracket.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885, Part II.B.5; same span

quotes.text: 6. Chimneys: There is one interior brick chimney centered on the east slope of the roof. The remnants of an exterior brick chimney located in the southwest corner of the roof‘s west slope are apparent, but it no longer exists.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885, Part II.B.6; the marker '(Page 12)' follows

quotes.text: a. Shape, covering: The side-gable roof is moderately pitched, and is sheathed in composite shingles. The porch roof appears as an offset cross gable on the west façade.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885, Part II.B.8; the marker '(Page 13)' follows

quotes.text: b. Cornice, eaves: There is a moderate eave overhang, with the exception of the shallow, rectangular bay window
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-2885 (Page 13); the extract's chunk ends mid-sentence here
